messages:
anna-ml: Heads-up — after merging the mixed-precision calibration change, staging 13B latency regressed. can we triage?

mike-runtime: rough numbers and env?

anna-ml: A100, batch=1, p50 went from ~36ms to ~54ms. p99 up too. KV warmup seems particularly worse (first few tokens).

jay-kernels: that screams kernel-selector fallback. per-channel scales often force slower dequant paths if fused kernels don't support them. do you have selector logs?

anna-ml: yes, attached profile: https://staging-profiles/redwood/2180001111 (tar). selector shows many matmuls hitting int8_dequant path instead of fused_int8.

ci-bot: profile uploaded by anna-ml: https://staging-profiles/redwood/2180001111 (link)

sara-ops: is the regression uniform across model sizes?

anna-ml: 7B shows small bump, 13B large, 70B unaffected. tiling patterns matter.

leo-quant: what's the calibration config? per-channel vs per-tensor, dataset size, clipping?

anna-ml: per-channel, ~50k mixed chat+code samples, 1% tail clip, per-layer scale search on.

jay-kernels: large sample + code-heavy tails could generate extreme per-channel ranges. fused kernel assumes per-tensor scales for vectorized ops; per-channel triggers extra multiplies/reorders.

mike-runtime: also check runtime heuristic thresholds. maybe the selector thinks the dequant path is cheaper for short sequences due to microbench numbers.

anna-ml: selector logs indicate many small matmuls in the middle layers went to fallback. KV fill (early tokens) pay repeated overhead and amplify latency.

sara-ops: KV warmup is multiplicative: overhead per block repeats during prefix filling. small extra op costs add up.

leo-quant: quick experiment idea: compare two calibrations — current per-channel full dataset vs per-tensor small sample (2k chat-like, 0.5% clip). measure selector hit-rate and end-to-end p50/p99.

mike-runtime: agree. schedule both on a dedicated non-prod pool and capture kernel_selector metrics + KV timings.

sara-ops: queued both runs. marking as non-prod. will attach perf logs to ticket.

(Background run)

anna-ml: Run B (per-tensor, 2k chat, 0.5% clip) finished: p50 ~38-41ms, p99 closer to baseline. selector stayed on fused_int8 for ~80-90% of matmuls. throughput +12% vs per-channel run.

jay-kernels: that's a smoking gun. fused path retained when scales are per-tensor. quality trade?

leo-quant: quick eval on 500 prompts: per-channel(full) wins by ~0.6 points on our internal metric. per-tensor small loses a bit but within acceptable bounds for latency-sensitive PLG workloads.

mike-runtime: tradeoff summary: per-channel = better numeric fidelity, but can add 30-40% latency on hotpath due to kernel fallback and KV warmup. per-tensor small = much better latency with small quality hit.

anna-ml: proposal: default to per-tensor small sample for general deployments, provide opt-in per-channel for accuracy-critical customers. also add a model-aware heuristic.

jay-kernels: technical options: (1) runtime heuristic during calibration: run a synthetic microbench and if fused_kernel_hit_rate < threshold (eg 90%), prefer per-tensor; (2) longer-term: extend fused kernel to accept per-channel scales (harder). I'll take (1) as it's quicker.

mike-runtime: implement heuristic + tests. also add CI microbench that catches regressions where selector falls back and KV warmup penalty rises.

sara-ops: I'll coordinate rollout notes for Dedicated customers and ensure non-prod tests run across 7B/13B/70B to avoid false positives.

leo-quant: additional idea: try "per-channel-lite" — per-channel but aggressive percentile clipping per-channel to dampen outliers. might keep accuracy gains while preserving fused hits. worth experiments.

anna-ml: I'll run extended evals (10k prompts) for the chosen default and the per-channel opt-in to quantify worst-case diffs. will update ticket with numbers.

mike-runtime: can someone open PRs: runtime heuristic, CI microbench, and calibration policy doc for SEs?

jay-kernels: opening PR for selector heuristic + microbench tests now.

anna-ml: drafting calibration policy: default sample 2k chat-like, 0.5% tail clip, per-channel opt-in with note about perf costs. will put draft in runbooks repo.

ci-bot: issue created: INF-4123 - mixed-precision calib/kernelfallback microbench + runtime heuristic tests

sara-ops: once PRs land, let's run canary on a small set of Dedicated customers after notifying them.

leo-quant: and let's add a small automated check during model onboarding: if model tiling or width suggests fused fragility, flag the default to per-tensor.

mike-runtime: good. also add a small regression test that simulates KV warmup to catch repeated per-block overheads.

anna-ml: thanks all — great triage. I'll paste full perf tables into INF-4123 and link the draft policy. ping here if you find other odd model interactions.

sara-ops: closing the loop for now. :thumbsup:

ci-bot: linked ticket: https://staging-tickets/redwood/INF-4123

leo-quant: thanks everyone. let's follow up after extended evals. :rocket:
